name: Atlas LV-3B
dispatch: If the Redstone was the cautious step, the Atlas was the leap. It was America's first intercontinental missile, and it reached orbital speed by being audaciously, almost alarmingly light: its skin was so thin that the rocket had to be kept pressurised like a balloon just to stand up without crumpling. Man-rating that — trusting a person to a missile that would collapse if you let the pressure drop — was the hard call that separated Mercury's suborbital half from its orbital one. Every American orbital flight of the program rode this thin steel balloon, and it is why Glenn, Carpenter, Schirra, and Cooper circled the Earth while Shepard and Grissom only touched the edge of it.
description: Atlas LV-3B is a orbital launcher built by Convair in USA. Lifted Mercury astronauts to orbit. Retired after first flight in 1962.
